stem: Find the value of the polynomial \(p(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 5\) for \(x = 2\).
solution:
Polynomial \(p(x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 5\)
Put \(x = 2\) in the given polynomial,
\(\therefore p(2) = 2 \times 2^2 - 3 \times 2 + 5\)
\(= 2 \times 4 - 6 + 5\)
\(= 8 - 6 + 5\)
\(\therefore p(2) = 7\)

\(p(y) = 2y^3 - 2y + \sqrt{7}\)
\(\therefore p(-2) = 2 \times (-2)^3 - 2 \times (-2) + \sqrt{7}\)
\(= 2 \times (-8) - 2 \times (-2) + \sqrt{7}\)
\(= -16 + 4 + \sqrt{7}\)
\(= -12 + \sqrt{7}\)
\(\therefore\) For \(y = -2\) the value of polynomial is \(-12 + \sqrt{7}\).

stem: If the value of the polynomial \(m^2 - am + 7\) for \(m = -1\) is 10, then find the value of \(a\).
solution:
\(p(m) = m^2 - am + 7\)
\(\therefore p(-1) = (-1)^2 - a \times (-1) + 7\)
\(= 1 + a + 7\)
\(= 8 + a\)
But \(p(-1) = 10\) (given.)
\(\therefore 8 + a = 10\)
\(\therefore a = 10 - 8\)
\(\therefore a = 2\)

stem: For \(x = 0\) find the value of the polynomial \(x^2 - 5x + 5\).
Divide \(p(x) = (4x^2 - x + 2)\) by \((x + 1)\), and verify that the remainder equals the value of \(p(x)\) at \(x = -1\).
solution:
Dividend polynomial \(= 4x^2 - x + 2\); Divisor polynomial \(= x + 1\)
By long division the quotient is \(4x - 5\) and the remainder is 7. ...... (I)

By the synthetic method — coefficient form of \(p(x)\) is \((4, -1, 2)\), and the opposite of 1 is \(-1\) :

| \(-1\) | 4 | \(-1\) | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
|  |  | \(-4\) | 5 |
|  | 4 | \(-5\) | 7 |

Quotient \(= 4x - 5\), Remainder \(= 7\)

Now put \(x = -1\) in the dividend polynomial :
\(p(x) = 4x^2 - x + 2\)
\(\therefore p(-1) = 4 \times (-1)^2 - (-1) + 2 = 4 \times 1 + 1 + 2 = 7\)
\(\therefore\) the value of the polynomial \(p(x)\) for \(x = -1\) is 7. ...... (II)
From (I) and (II), the remainder when \(p(x)\) is divided by \((x + 1)\) and the value \(p(-1)\) are equal — which is the Remainder theorem.

stem: Divide \(x^4 - 5x^2 - 4x\) by \(x + 3\) and find the remainder.
By using remainder theorem divide the polynomial \(x^3 - 2x^2 - 4x - 1\) by \(x - 1\) and find the remainder.
solution:
\(p(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 - 4x - 1\)
Divisor \(= x - 1\) \(\therefore\) take \(x = 1\)
\(\therefore\) Remainder \(= p(1) = 1^3 - 2 \times 1^2 - 4 \times 1 - 1\) ...(by remainder theorem)
\(= 1 - 2 \times 1 - 4 - 1\)
\(p(1) = 1 - 2 - 4 - 1 = -6\)
\(\therefore\) Remainder \(= -6\)
